Posterior functionals of the variance components

Source: R/vpredict.R
vpredict.Rd

The exact posterior of any function of the fitted variance components: a heritability, a genetic correlation, a variance ratio, a repeatability. Each functional is written as a two-sided formula whose left side names the result and whose right side is an expression over the component names that summary() reports.

Usage

vpredict(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexybayes'
vpredict(object, ..., n_draws = 1000L, prob = 0.95, draws = FALSE)

Arguments

object

A fitted flexybayes model.

...

One or more two-sided formulas, name ~ expression.

n_draws

Number of posterior draws to evaluate over.

prob

Width of the credible interval.

draws

When TRUE, return the matrix of functional draws (one column per functional) instead of the summary.

Value

A data.frame with one row per functional and the columns functional, estimate (posterior mean), median, std.error (posterior standard deviation), conf.low and conf.high. With draws = TRUE, a numeric matrix of draws instead.

Details

Components are on the standard-deviation scale, as everywhere else in this package, so a variance ratio squares them. Writing a name the fit does not carry is refused, and the refusal lists the names it does.

The interval is a quantile interval of the functional's own posterior. Where the delta method would put a heritability's interval below zero, this one cannot: every draw of sd_g^2 / (sd_g^2 + sigma^2) lies in [0, 1], so the interval does too.

The method is also registered on sommer's vpredict() generic, so vpredict(fit, ...) reaches it when sommer is attached after flexyBayes.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit <- flexybayes(yield ~ 1, random = ~ gen, data = trial)
vpredict(fit, h2 ~ sd_gen^2 / (sd_gen^2 + sigma^2))
} # }
